Initiated by: AFS-50 Change:
1 PURPOSE OF THIS ADVISORY CIRCULAR (AC). This AC transmits an updated
schedule of charges for services of Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Flight
Standards Service (FS) aviation safety inspectors (ASI) outside the United States. On
April 19, 1995, the FAA amended Title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations (14 CFR)
part 187 (60 Federal Register (FR) 19628-01, April 19, 1995, Fees for Certification
Services and Approvals Performed Outside the United States), which established the
methodology for determining these charges. The rule provided that the FAA would
publish these fees in an AC. Refer to 14 CFR part 187 appendix A.
2 EFFECTIVE DATE. The effective date of this AC is October 1, 2026.
3 WHAT THIS AC CANCELS. AC 187-1U, Flight Standards Service Schedule of
Charges Outside the United States, dated July 9, 2025, is canceled.
4 RELATED 14 CFR REFERENCES. Each charge listed in Appendix 1, Schedule of
Services, Flight Standards Service, Schedule of Charges Outside the United States, refers
to an FAA activity described in FAA regulations. Listed beside each category of service
and charge is the specific regulatory reference. Generally, these charges refer to 14 CFR:
• Parts 60, 61, 63, 65, 133, 135, and 137 (Airman Certification);
• Parts 141, 142, 145, and 147 (Air Agency Certification);
• Part 183, Representatives of the Administrator; and
• Part 187 Appendix A, Methodology for Computation of Fees for Certification
Services Performed Outside the United States.
5 APPENDIX CHANGES. The FAA plans to review the actual costs incurred in the
services listed in Appendix 1 at the beginning of each fiscal year (FY). The FAA will do
this using the same fee methodology described in 14 CFR part 187 appendix A. The FAA
will amend the schedule of charges on an annual basis to either increase or decrease fees,
as needed. The FAA will publish each amended schedule in the FR and as a revision to
this AC.

6 COMMENTS AND INQUIRIES. Direct comments or inquiries regarding this AC to: Federal Aviation Administration Flight Standards Service International Program Division, AFS-50 800 Independence Avenue, SW Washington, DC 20591 7 AC FEEDBACK FORM. For your convenience, the AC Feedback Form is the last page of this AC. Note any deficiencies found, clarifications needed, or suggested improvements regarding the contents of this AC on the Feedback Form. Timothy R. Adams for Hugh J. Thomas Executive Director, Flight Standards Service

I. TRANSPORTATION AND SUBSISTENCE CHARGES
All Categories of Services
Transportation and subsistence will be assessed to applicants in
addition to the charge published below for certification actions
requiring travel from the duty station city.
Title 5 of the Code of Federal Regulations (5 CFR) part 2635,
Standards of Ethical Conduct for Employees of the Executive
Branch, and as set forth in the Federal Aviation Administration
(FAA) Standards of Conduct in FAA Human Resources Policy
Manual, Volume 4, prohibits employees, with certain
exceptions, from accepting any gifts, favors, gratuities, or any
other thing of monetary value, including free transportation,
from any person or company that is subject to FAA regulations
that has or is seeking to have contractual relations with the FAA
or that has interests that might be affected by the performance or
nonperformance of the duties of the particular employee.
The only permissible exceptions to this for FAA employees
performing services under Title 14 of the Code of Federal
Regulations (14 CFR) part 187 appendix A, and its
implementing advisory circular (AC) 187-1, are for: 1) meals at
a facility where such meals are available to all individuals at the
facility at no charge, and 2) “in-kind” contributions of ground
transportation services to and from facilities only when there are
bona fide personnel security risks associated with conveyance
by local transportation that have been verified by the applicable
United States Embassy or Consulate and the applicant offers to
provide the transportation.
In these cases, the United States Embassy or Consulate must
accept the intended “in-kind” transportation method as
sufficient to mitigate the perceived risks.
